source "https://rubygems.org"
git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

ruby "3.3.6"

# Bundle edge Rails instead: gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
gem "rails", "7.0.8.7"
gem "concurrent-ruby", "1.3.4"

# The original asset pipeline for Rails [https://github.com/rails/sprockets-rails]
gem "sprockets-rails"

# Use postgresql as the database for Active Record
gem "pg", "1.6.0"

# Use the Puma web server [https://github.com/puma/puma]
gem "puma", "~> 5.0"

# Use JavaScript with ESM import maps [https://github.com/rails/importmap-rails]
gem "importmap-rails"

# Hotwire's SPA-like page accelerator [https://turbo.hotwired.dev]
gem "turbo-rails"

# Hotwire's modest JavaScript framework [https://stimulus.hotwired.dev]
gem "stimulus-rails"

# Build JSON APIs with ease [https://github.com/rails/jbuilder]
gem "jbuilder"

# Paginate the note list [https://github.com/ddnexus/pagy]
gem "pagy", "8.6.3"

# Run Active Job on Redis through Sidekiq [https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq]
gem "sidekiq", "6.5.12"
gem "redis", "4.8.1"

# Request citation metadata over HTTP [https://github.com/lostisland/faraday]
gem "faraday", "1.10.4"

# Use Kredis to get higher-level data types in Redis [https://github.com/rails/kredis]
# gem "kredis"

# Use Active Model has_secure_password [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_model_basics.html#securepassword]
gem "bcrypt", "~> 3.1.7"

# Windows does not include zoneinfo files, so bundle the tzinfo-data gem
gem "tzinfo-data", platforms: %i[ mingw mswin x64_mingw jruby ]

# Reduces boot times through caching; required in config/boot.rb
gem "bootsnap", require: false

# Use Sass to process CSS
# gem "sassc-rails"

# Use Active Storage variants [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#transforming-images]
# gem "image_processing", "~> 1.2"

group :development, :test do
  # See https://guides.rubyonrails.org/debugging_rails_applications.html#debugging-with-the-debug-gem
  gem "debug", platforms: %i[ mri mingw x64_mingw ]
end

group :development do
  # Use console on exceptions pages [https://github.com/rails/web-console]
  gem "web-console"

  # Add speed badges [https://github.com/MiniProfiler/rack-mini-profiler]
  # gem "rack-mini-profiler"

  # Speed up commands on slow machines / big apps [https://github.com/rails/spring]
  # gem "spring"
end

group :test do
  # Use system testing [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/testing.html#system-testing]
  gem "capybara"
  gem "selenium-webdriver"

  # Rails 7.0's test runner is incompatible with Minitest 6
  gem "minitest", "~> 5.25"
end

# Architecture

## Starting point

Margin Notes is a reading-notebook application. Implemented so far:

- A reader (`User`) signs in with email and password through `has_secure_password`.
  `SessionsController` stores only the user ID in the Rails session.
  `ApplicationController#require_sign_in` protects the application's other
  controllers, but not Rails' Active Storage controllers.
- A reader owns `Notebook`s, and each `Note` belongs to one notebook. A note's
  owner is its notebook's owner, so `User#notes` (through notebooks) is the
  authorized note scope. There is no separate `user_id` on notes.
- `NotesController#index` serves `/notes` and its `/journal` alias. It lists the
  reader's notes newest first with an ID tie-breaker, and supports title search
  and notebook and status filters. `show` renders one note's rich body.
- Pagy 8.6.3 paginates that filtered list after ordering, 10 notes per page by
  default. The search form offers 5, 10, 25, or 50 as the `per_page` URL
  parameter. Larger requested sizes are capped at 50. Next and previous links keep
  the filters and page size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric page shows the
  first page, and a page past the end shows the last page. The form never sends
  an invalid size. A blank, zero, negative, or nonnumeric `per_page` in a URL is
  not handled, and Pagy raises `Pagy::VariableError`.
- A note's body is Action Text (`has_rich_text :body`), edited with Trix.
  Attachments are Active Storage blobs on the local Disk service. `Note` rejects
  saves that embed a blob over 1 MB. Direct uploads store blobs before this
  validation, without a size limit. Rejected or abandoned uploads remain
  unattached, and nothing purges them. No image processor is installed, so images
  use the original blobs, not variants. A migration converted existing plain-text
  bodies to escaped rich text.
- Action Text sanitizes rich text when it renders. The
  [Action Text initializer](config/initializers/action_text.rb) adds
  `details`/`summary` to the default allowlist for collapsible excerpts. Trix
  does not support those elements. Stored excerpts render as collapsible content,
  but saving them through the editor permanently flattens that structure, even
  when only tags or highlight change.
- Note tags are a JSON array in a text column, entered as a comma-separated
  list (`Note#tag_list`). The highlight color is `color` in the `settings` jsonb
  column, which the form edits as `highlight_color`.
- `NotebooksController#edit`/`update` are notebook settings. The slug is derived
  from the name on creation and is read-only afterward (`attr_readonly`). The
  settings form resubmits it unchanged. The export heading is stored in the
  serialized `preferences` hash. Markdown exports use both.
- A reader imports a CSV into one owned notebook. `ImportPreviewsController`
  reads the upload and renders a preview without saving. The preview page sends
  the CSV text back in a hidden field, and `ImportsController#create` reads and
  validates it again rather than trusting the preview. `Import#apply` saves the
  import and each row's note in one transaction. If any row cannot be saved,
  nothing from the batch remains. The receipt page and its CSV download list
  each imported note's title and DOI. Submitting the same preview twice creates
  two imports.
- `Import` accepts one format: UTF-8 CSV with the header row
  `title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch`, at most 100 notes and 100 KB.
  Only the title is required. Previews identify rows by their source line, so a
  quoted multi-line body keeps the line where its row starts. Body HTML takes the
  same Action Text assignment and render-time sanitization as the editor.
- A `Citation` is identified by its DOI, the table's `doi` primary key, and is
  shared by every reader who cites it. A DOI is stored as given apart from
  surrounding whitespace, so case variants are different citations. Rows in one
  import share a new citation. Two simultaneous imports that introduce the same
  new DOI can conflict; the losing request fails with a server error and saves
  nothing. A reader's annotation and optional reminder epoch belong to the note,
  not the citation. Annotations are plain text in both the preview and note page;
  line breaks are preserved on the note page, but markup is displayed literally.
  Applying an import does not schedule its reminders; the reader schedules each
  one from its note.
- A reader can also enter a DOI on the note form (`Note#doi=`), which cites the
  shared citation with that exact, trimmed DOI or creates it.
- A reader requests metadata for the citation on one of their notes with
  `CitationEnrichmentsController#create`, nested under the note. It resolves the
  note through `current_user.notes`, so another reader's note, or a note without
  a DOI, is a 404. `Citation#request_enrichment` marks the citation pending and
  queues `CitationEnrichmentJob`, unless a request is already pending. The job
  calls `Citation#enrich`, which stores the provider's title and source URL and
  marks the citation completed, or records a failure message. Metadata and
  status belong to the shared citation, so every note citing the DOI shows them.
  The note page shows the state; it does not update itself while pending.
- `Citation::Provider` is the HTTP client for the metadata provider. It reads
  its URL and basic-auth credentials from [config/secrets.yml](config/secrets.yml)
  through `Rails.application.secrets`; that file reads them from the environment.
  Faraday retries a GET once on 503. A 401, 403, or 404, or a response without a
  title and an http(s) URL, fails the enrichment at once. A 429 or 5xx, timeout,
  or connection failure raises `Citation::Provider::Unavailable`. The job retries
  that with `retry_on`, three attempts in all at exponentially longer waits, then
  records the failure instead of passing the error to Sidekiq's own retries. A
  persistently unavailable provider therefore receives at most six requests per
  enrichment request. A job that fails for another reason uses Sidekiq's retries
  and leaves the citation pending meanwhile.
- [bin/citation-provider](bin/citation-provider) is a deterministic local stand-in
  for the provider, used for development and demonstrations. No real provider or
  credentials are configured.
- A reader exports an owned notebook as Markdown from its exports page
  (`ExportsController`, nested under the notebook). `Notebook#request_export`
  saves a queued `Export`, then queues the native Sidekiq job `ExportJob` and
  stores its job ID, which the page shows. The export is committed before the
  job is queued so the worker can always load it. If Redis refuses the job, the
  export is removed and the request fails. Each request creates a new export.
- `Export#generate`, run by the worker, marks the export working with the
  notebook's note count, then writes the notes oldest first (creation time, then
  ID). The file starts with the notebook's export heading, or its name when none
  is set. Each note is a second-level heading with its title on one line,
  followed by its body as Action Text plain text. Markdown characters are not
  escaped. Progress is saved after each note. A retried job starts again from
  the first note. There is no failed state: while Sidekiq retries a failing job,
  the export shows as working and the reader can cancel it.
- Cancelling (`ExportCancellationsController`) sets a queued or working export's
  persisted status to cancelled under its row lock. The worker checks that status
  before each note and before completing, then stops and keeps no file. Completed
  and cancelled exports cannot be cancelled.
- The worker uploads the file to Active Storage (`<slug>.md`) before marking the
  export completed, so a completed export always has a file. It can be downloaded
  for 24 hours (`Export::AVAILABLE_FOR`). `ExportDownloadsController` resolves the
  export through the reader's notebook, so another reader's export is a 404, and
  checks `Export#downloadable?` on every request before any conditional response.
  An expired, cancelled, or unfinished export redirects to the exports page. The
  file is sent by the application, never by an Active Storage URL, with an ETag
  and Last-Modified from the stored file and `private, must-revalidate`.
  A failed upload can leave an unattached blob row without a stored file. Nothing
  cleans up those rows, and each failed retry can leave another one.
- The exports page caches each completed export's availability indicator as a
  fragment that expires at the export's deadline. The download action does not
  read that cache. The page does not update itself while an export is queued or
  working. Nothing purges expired files; they remain in storage.
- A notebook's activity page (`ActivityReportsController#show`, nested under the
  notebook and linked from the notebooks list) shows how many of its notes were
  created on each UTC date, newest date first. It is read-only and resolves the
  notebook through `current_user.notebooks`, so another reader's notebook is a
  404. `Notebook#daily_note_counts` groups the notes by `DATE(created_at)` in
  PostgreSQL and reads the rows with a raw `select_rows`, which returns each date
  as ISO 8601 text; the method parses it with `Date.iso8601`. Every status counts,
  and dates without notes are omitted. The report is derived from the notes that
  exist when it is requested, not an activity log: deleting a note lowers its
  date's count, and nothing records past counts.
- Each reader has a time zone (`User#time_zone`, UTC by default), chosen on the
  account settings page (`AccountsController`). Reminder times use it. Digests
  follow UTC days, and other pages still show times in UTC.
- A note's reminder is its `reminder_epoch`, a time in seconds since 1970, set by
  an import or by the reader. `RemindersController#create`, nested under the
  note, reads a date and time the reader entered in their time zone
  (`User#local_time`), or, with none, uses the stored time. `Note#schedule_reminder`
  queues `NoteReminderJob` for that time with `set(wait_until:)` and stores the
  job's ID, under the note's row lock, so a failed enqueue keeps the earlier
  reminder. A local time that does not exist because of a daylight saving change
  moves forward, and an ambiguous one takes its first occurrence. A time in the
  past is sent as soon as a worker runs the job.
- Scheduling again, or postponing (`ReminderPostponementsController`), replaces the
  reminder. Earlier jobs stay in Sidekiq's schedule, but send nothing: when a job
  runs, `Note#send_reminder` takes the row lock and emails the reader only if its
  job ID is still the note's and the reminder has not been sent, then records
  `reminder_sent_at`. The note page shows whether a reminder is imported but not
  scheduled, scheduled, or sent. A job that fails after the email is written can
  send it again when Sidekiq retries it.
- Postponing moves the reminder 24 elapsed hours later. The note page previews
  that time as `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`, which keeps the reminder's UTC
  offset. Across a daylight saving change the preview shows the right instant,
  but at a different offset and wall-clock time from the postponed reminder.
- A reader requests a digest of their ready notes from the notes page
  (`DigestsController`). `User#request_digest` reserves the reader's ID in a
  Redis set for the request's UTC date
  (`digest_requests:YYYY-MM-DD`, kept for two days) and queues `DigestJob` with
  the reader, the request time in the reader's zone, and the share of their notes
  that are ready, as a `BigDecimal`. A reader whose ID is already in the day's set
  is told the digest was already requested. If the job cannot be queued, the
  reservation is removed and the error raised, so the request fails and can be
  repeated. The reservation prevents repeated requests, not repeated emails:
  Sidekiq can run a job more than once. Each request logs redis-rb's deprecation
  warning for a single-member `sadd`, and Sidekiq warns that the job's arguments
  are not native JSON types, because of the `BigDecimal`.
- Sidekiq stores the job's arguments as JSON. Active Job 7.0 sends the request
  time with its UTC offset but deserializes it in the worker's zone, UTC, and the
  completion arrives as a decimal string such as `"0.6667"`. `DigestMailer` lists
  the reader's ready notes last updated during that UTC day, and dates the digest
  by it. The content day matches the reservation's day, even near local midnight.
  A digest is a snapshot when its job runs; notes updated afterward are not sent
  in a second digest for that UTC day.
- The mailers write plain-text email. Development writes each recipient's email
  to `tmp/mails` (Action Mailer's file delivery); tests use the `:test` delivery
  method. Production has no delivery method or link host configured.
- Active Storage serves blobs through signed URLs from its own controllers. Those
  URLs are not checked against the signed-in reader. The embedded blob redirect
  URLs do not expire, although the Disk-service URLs they redirect to do.
  The direct-upload controller checks CSRF, not sign-in; the public sign-in page
  supplies a CSRF token to anonymous clients. This sample has no private-file
  access policy or upload-abuse protection for a public deployment.

These conventions guide further features without prescribing a schema in advance.

The initial runtime is Ruby 3.3.6 and Rails 7.0.8.7 with Rails 7.0 defaults.
[Gemfile](Gemfile), [Gemfile.lock](Gemfile.lock), [.ruby-version](.ruby-version), and
[config/application.rb](config/application.rb) are the executable sources of truth.

- PostgreSQL is the application database. Use Active Record and migrations for
  application-owned records, constraints, indexes, and transactions.
- ERB renders HTML. The generated app includes Sprockets, importmap, Turbo, and
  Stimulus. Jbuilder is available for requested JSON representations, but an HTML
  feature does not automatically need a JSON API.
- Rails includes the mailer, job, storage, and cable frameworks. Their presence
  does not mean broadcasts are implemented features. Email is sent only for
  reminders and digests, and is not delivered outside development's files. File
  uploads exist only as rich-text attachments.

  digest reservations; it is not an application cache. The generated production
  cable configuration names Redis. That configuration is not a verified deployment.

## Prefer Rails objects with clear responsibilities

Use the framework's ordinary directories and interfaces:

| Responsibility | Home |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP verbs, paths, and resource nesting | `config/routes.rb` |
| Parameter selection, authorized lookup, response negotiation | `app/controllers/` |
| Persistent state and domain operations | `app/models/` |
| A cohesive capability of one model | A namespace beneath `app/models/` |
| Behavior genuinely shared across models | `app/models/concerns/` |
| HTML, Turbo stream, and JSON representations | `app/views/` |
| Presentation helpers | `app/helpers/` |
| Browser interaction around rendered HTML | `app/javascript/controllers/` |
| Background execution and retry boundary | `app/jobs/` |
| Mail composition | `app/mailers/` and its views |

     1	# A work identified by its DOI, shared by every reader who cites it. Readers'
     2	# own annotations stay on their notes. Its metadata, and the state of the latest
     3	# request for it, are shared too.
     4	class Citation < ApplicationRecord
     5	  has_many :notes, foreign_key: :citation_doi
     6	
     7	  enum :enrichment_status, { pending: 0, completed: 1, failed: 2 }, prefix: :enrichment
     8	
     9	  validates :doi, format: { with: %r{\A10\.\d{4,9}/\S+\z} }
    10	
    11	  # Marks the citation pending and queues a metadata lookup, unless one is
    12	  # already pending. Returns whether a lookup was queued. The job is queued under
    13	  # the row lock, so a failed enqueue rolls back the pending state.
    14	  def request_enrichment
    15	    with_lock do
    16	      if enrichment_pending?
    17	        false
    18	      else
    19	        update!(enrichment_status: :pending, enrichment_error: nil)
    20	        CitationEnrichmentJob.perform_later(self)
    21	        true
    22	      end
    23	    end
    24	  end
    25	
    26	  # Asks the provider for this DOI's metadata. A permanent refusal marks the
    27	  # enrichment failed; an unavailable provider raises so the job can retry.
    28	  def enrich
    29	    metadata = Provider.new.lookup(doi)
    30	    record_enrichment(title: metadata.title, source_url: metadata.source_url, enrichment_status: :completed, enrichment_error: nil)
    31	  rescue Provider::Error => error
    32	    fail_enrichment(error.message)
    33	  end
    34	
    35	  def fail_enrichment(reason)
    36	    record_enrichment(enrichment_status: :failed, enrichment_error: reason)
    37	  end
    38	
    39	  private
    40	    # The job can load this citation before the request that queued it commits.
    41	    # Taking the row lock waits for that commit and reloads, so the result is
    42	    # written even when it equals the values loaded earlier.
    43	    def record_enrichment(attributes)
    44	      with_lock { update!(attributes) }
    45	    end

     1	# A Markdown file of one notebook's notes, written by ExportJob. The reader can
     2	# cancel it while it is queued or working; the worker checks between notes and
     3	# stops. A completed file can be downloaded until it expires.
     4	class Export < ApplicationRecord
     5	  AVAILABLE_FOR = 24.hours
     6	
     7	  belongs_to :notebook
     8	  has_one_attached :file
     9	
    10	  enum :status, { queued: 0, working: 1, completed: 2, cancelled: 3 }
    11	
    12	  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
    13	
    14	  def cancellable?
    15	    queued? || working?
    16	  end
    17	
    18	  # Cancels a queued or working export. Returns whether it was cancelled.
    19	  def cancel
    20	    with_lock do
    21	      if cancellable?
    22	        update!(status: :cancelled)
    23	      else
    24	        false
    25	      end
    26	    end
    27	  end
    28	
    29	  # Writes the notebook's notes, oldest first, under its export heading. Progress
    30	  # is saved after each note. A cancelled export stops before the next note and
    31	  # keeps no file.
    32	  def generate
    33	    notes = notebook.notes.with_rich_text_body.order(:created_at, :id).to_a
    34	    return unless start(notes.size)
    35	
    36	    fragments = ["# #{notebook.export_heading || notebook.name}\n"]
    37	    notes.each_with_index do |note, index|
    38	      fragments << markdown_for(note)
    39	      return unless record_progress(index + 1)
    40	    end
    41	
    42	    finish(fragments.sum)
    43	  end
    44	
    45	  # The authoritative check for downloading the file.
    46	  def downloadable?
    47	    completed? && expires_at.future?
    48	  end
    49	
    50	  private
    51	    # A retried job starts again from the first note.
    52	    def start(total)
    53	      with_lock do
    54	        update!(status: :working, processed_notes_count: 0, total_notes_count: total) if cancellable?
    55	      end
    56	    end
    57	
    58	    def record_progress(count)
    59	      with_lock do
    60	        update!(processed_notes_count: count) unless cancelled?
    61	      end
    62	    end
    63	
    64	    # The file is stored before the export is marked completed, so a completed
    65	    # export always has one.
    66	    def finish(markdown)
    67	      blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: StringIO.new(markdown),
    68	        filename: "#{notebook.slug}.md", content_type: "text/markdown")
    69	
    70	      completed = with_lock do
    71	        update!(file: blob, status: :completed, expires_at: AVAILABLE_FOR.from_now) unless cancelled?
    72	      end
    73	
    74	      blob.purge unless completed
    75	    end
    76	
    77	    def markdown_for(note)
    78	      body = note.body.to_plain_text.strip
    79	      markdown = "\n## #{note.title.squish}\n"
    80	      markdown += "\n#{body}\n" if body.present?
    81	      markdown
    82	    end
    83	end

    53	    transaction do

    77	
    78	      reader = CSV.new(csv.delete_prefix("\uFEFF").encode(universal_newline: true))

    80	      next_line = 1

     4	class Citation::Provider

     9	  class Unavailable < StandardError; end
    10	
    11	  Metadata = Struct.new(:title, :source_url)
    12	
    13	  def initialize(settings = Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider.to_h)
    14	    @url, @user, @password = settings.values_at(:url, :user, :password)
    15	  end
    16	
    17	  def lookup(doi)
    18	    raise Error, "No citation provider is configured" if @url.blank?
    19	
    20	    response = connection.get("works", doi: doi)
    21	
    22	    case response.status
    23	    when 200 then metadata_from(response.body)
    24	    when 401, 403 then raise Error, "The provider rejected the configured credentials (HTTP #{response.status})"
    25	    when 404 then raise Error, "The provider has no record of this DOI"
    26	    when 429, 500..599 then raise Unavailable, "The provider is unavailable (HTTP #{response.status})"
    27	    else raise Error, "The provider gave an unexpected response (HTTP #{response.status})"
    28	    end
    29	  rescue Faraday::ConnectionFailed, Faraday::TimeoutError => error

    31	  end

    34	    # Retries a GET once on 503 before reporting the provider unavailable.
    35	    def connection

    37	        faraday.request :retry, max: 1, retry_statuses: [503]

    39	      end
    40	    end

    42	    def metadata_from(body)
    43	      attributes = JSON.parse(body)
    44	      title, source_url = attributes["title"], attributes["url"] if attributes.is_a?(Hash)
    45

    47	        Metadata.new(title.strip, source_url)

    50	      end

    53	    end

# frozen_string_literal: true

# :markup: markdown

require "rails"
require "action_controller/railtie"
require "active_record/railtie"
require "active_storage/engine"

require "action_text"
require "action_text/trix"

module ActionText
  class Engine < Rails::Engine
    isolate_namespace ActionText
    config.eager_load_namespaces << ActionText

    config.action_text = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
    config.action_text.attachment_tag_name = "action-text-attachment"
    config.autoload_once_paths = %W(
      #{root}/app/helpers
      #{root}/app/models
    )

    initializer "action_text.deprecator", before: :load_environment_config do |app|
      app.deprecators[:action_text] = ActionText.deprecator
    end

    initializer "action_text.attribute" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
        include ActionText::Attribute
        prepend ActionText::Encryption
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.asset" do
      if Rails.application.config.respond_to?(:assets)
        Rails.application.config.assets.precompile += %w( actiontext.js actiontext.esm.js )
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.attachable" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_storage_blob) do
        include ActionText::Attachable

        def previewable_attachable?
          representable?
        end

        def attachable_plain_text_representation(caption = nil)
          "[#{caption || filename}]"
        end

        def to_trix_content_attachment_partial_path
          nil
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.helper" do
      %i[action_controller_base action_mailer].each do |base|
        ActiveSupport.on_load(base) do
          helper ActionText::Engine.helpers
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.renderer" do
      %i[action_controller_base action_mailer].each do |base|
        ActiveSupport.on_load(base) do
          around_action do |controller, action|
            ActionText::Content.with_renderer(controller, &action)
          end
        end
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.system_test_helper" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_dispatch_system_test_case) do
        require "action_text/system_test_helper"
        include ActionText::SystemTestHelper
      end
    end

    initializer "action_text.configure" do |app|
      ActionText::Attachment.tag_name = app.config.action_text.attachment_tag_name
    end

    config.after_initialize do |app|
      if klass = app.config.action_text.sanitizer_vendor
        ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_view) do
          ActionText::ContentHelper.sanitizer = klass.safe_list_sanitizer.new
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

*Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated override of `Enumerable#sum`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Deprecated initializing a `ActiveSupport::Cache::MemCacheStore` with an instance of `Dalli::Client`.

    This resulted in an accumulation of open file descriptors, which could
    cause errors if the limit is reached.

    *Sam Bostock*

*   Fix `Time#change` and `Time#advance` for times around the end of Daylight
    Saving Time.

    Previously, when `Time#change` or `Time#advance` constructed a time inside
    the final stretch of Daylight Saving Time (DST), the non-DST offset would
    always be chosen for local times:

    ```ruby
    # DST ended just before 2021-11-07 2:00:00 AM in US/Eastern.
    ENV["TZ"] = "US/Eastern"

    time = Time.local(2021, 11, 07, 00, 59, 59) + 1
    # => 2021-11-07 01:00:00 -0400
    time.change(day: 07)
    # => 2021-11-07 01:00:00 -0500
    time.advance(seconds: 0)
    # => 2021-11-07 01:00:00 -0500

    time = Time.local(2021, 11, 06, 01, 00, 00)
    # => 2021-11-06 01:00:00 -0400
    to mutate a shared default object.

    *Jonathan Hefner*

*   Add `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time` config to `ActiveSupport::Cache::Store`

    Specifies if an `ArgumentError` should be raised if `Rails.cache` `fetch` or
    `write` are given an invalid `expires_at` or `expires_in` time.

    Options are `true`, and `false`. If `false`, the exception will be reported
    as `handled` and logged instead. Defaults to `true` if `config.load_defaults >= 7.1`.

     *Trevor Turk*

*   `ActiveSupport::Cache::Store#fetch` now passes an options accessor to the block.

    *Steven Harman*

*   Deprecate preserving the pre-Ruby 2.4 behavior of `to_time`

    With Ruby 2.4+ the default for +to_time+ changed from converting to the
    local system time to preserving the offset of the receiver. At the time Rails
    supported older versions of Ruby so a compatibility layer was added to assist
    in the migration process. From Rails 5.0 new applications have defaulted to
    the Ruby 2.4+ behavior and since Rails 7.0 now only supports Ruby 2.7+
    this compatibility layer can be safely removed.

    To minimize any noise generated the deprecation warning only appears when the
    setting is configured to `false` as that is the only scenario where the
    removal of the compatibility layer has any effect.

    *Andrew White*

*   `Pathname.blank?` only returns true for `Pathname.new("")`

    *Jean Boussier*

*   Updating Astana with Western Kazakhstan TZInfo identifier.

    *Damian Nelson*

*   Add filename support for `ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?`.

*   Don't execute i18n watcher on boot. It shouldn't catch any file changes initially,
    and unnecessarily slows down boot of applications with lots of translations.

    *Gannon McGibbon*, *David Stosik*

*   Fix `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess#stringify_keys` to stringify all keys not just symbols.

    Previously:

    ```ruby
    { 1 => 2 }.with_indifferent_access.stringify_keys[1] # => 2
    ```

    After this change:

    ```ruby
    { 1 => 2 }.with_indifferent_access.stringify_keys["1"] # => 2
    ```

    This change can be seen as a bug fix, but since it behaved like this for a very long time, we're deciding
    to not backport the fix and to make the change in a major release.

    *Jean Boussier*

## Rails 8.0.0.beta1 (September 26, 2024) ##
    As is the case when trying to use an Integer or Float as a key, which is unsupported.

    *zzak*

*   Deprecate addition and since between two `Time` and `ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone`.

    Previously adding time instances together such as `10.days.ago + 10.days.ago` or `10.days.ago.since(10.days.ago)` produced a nonsensical future date. This behavior is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.1.

    *Nick Schwaderer*

class Range # :nodoc:
  # Optimize range sum to use arithmetic progression if a block is not given and
  # we have a range of numeric values.
  def sum(initial_value = 0)
    if block_given? || !(first.is_a?(Integer) && last.is_a?(Integer))
      super
    else
      actual_last = exclude_end? ? (last - 1) : last
      if actual_last >= first
        sum = initial_value || 0
        sum + (actual_last - first + 1) * (actual_last + first) / 2
      else
        initial_value || 0
      end
    end
  end
  #
  # The latter is a shortcut for:
  #
  #   payments.inject(0) { |sum, p| sum + p.price }
  #
  # It can also calculate the sum without the use of a block.
  #
  #   [5, 15, 10].sum # => 30
  #   ['foo', 'bar'].sum('') # => "foobar"
  #   [[1, 2], [3, 1, 5]].sum([]) # => [1, 2, 3, 1, 5]
  #
  # The default sum of an empty list is zero. You can override this default:
  #
  #   [].sum(Payment.new(0)) { |i| i.amount } # => Payment.new(0)
  def sum(identity = nil, &block)
    if identity
      _original_sum_with_required_identity(identity, &block)
    elsif block_given?
      map(&block).sum
    else
      first = true

      reduce(nil) do |sum, value|
        if first
          first = false

          unless value.is_a?(Numeric) || value.respond_to?(:coerce)
            ActiveSupport::Deprecation.warn(<<-MSG.squish)
              Rails 7.0 has deprecated Enumerable.sum in favor of Ruby's native implementation available since 2.4.
              Sum of non-numeric elements requires an initial argument.
            MSG
          end
          value
        else
          sum + value
        end
    delete_if { |_k, v| v.blank? }
  end
end

## Rails 7.2.0 (August 09, 2024) ##

*   All tests now respect the `active_job.queue_adapter` config.

    Previously if you had set `config.active_job.queue_adapter` in your `config/application.rb`
    or `config/environments/test.rb` file, the adapter you selected was previously not used consistently
    across all tests. In some tests your adapter would be used, but other tests would use the `TestAdapter`.

    In Rails 7.2, all tests will respect the `queue_adapter` config if provided. If no config is provided,
    the `TestAdapter` will continue to be used.

    See [#48585](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/48585) for more details.

    *Alex Ghiculescu*

*   Make Active Job transaction aware when used conjointly with Active Record.

    A common mistake with Active Job is to enqueue jobs from inside a transaction,
    causing them to potentially be picked and ran by another process, before the
    transaction is committed, which may result in various errors.

    ```ruby
    Topic.transaction do
      topic = Topic.create(...)
      NewTopicNotificationJob.perform_later(topic)
    end
    ```

    Now Active Job will automatically defer the enqueuing to after the transaction is committed,
    and drop the job if the transaction is rolled back.

    Various queue implementations can choose to disable this behavior, and users can disable it,
    or force it on a per job basis:

    ```ruby
    class NewTopicNotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = :never # or `:always` or `:default`
    end
    ```

    *Jean Boussier*, *Cristian Bica*

*   Do not trigger immediate loading of `ActiveJob::Base` when loading `ActiveJob::TestHelper`.

    *Maxime Réty*

*   Preserve the serialized timezone when deserializing `ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone` arguments.

    *Joshua Young*

*   Remove deprecated `:exponentially_longer` value for the `:wait` in `retry_on`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated support to set numeric values to `scheduled_at` attribute.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Deprecate `Rails.application.config.active_job.use_big_decimal_serializer`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated primitive serializer for `BigDecimal` arguments.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Do not trigger immediate loading of `ActiveJob::Base` when loading `ActiveJob::TestHelper`.

    *Maxime Réty*

*   Preserve the serialized timezone when deserializing `ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone` arguments.

    *Joshua Young*

*   Fix ActiveJob arguments serialization to correctly serialize String subclasses having custom serializers.

    *fatkodima*
## Rails 7.1.0.rc1 (September 27, 2023) ##

*   Set `scheduled_at` attribute as a Time object instead of epoch seconds, and serialize and deserialize the value
    when enqueued. Assigning a numeric/epoch value to scheduled_at= is deprecated; use a Time object instead.

    Deserializes `enqueued_at` as a Time instead of ISO8601 String.

    *Ben Sheldon*

*   Clarify the backoff strategy for the recommended `:wait` option when retrying jobs
*   Fix BigDecimal (de)serialization for adapters using JSON.

    Previously, BigDecimal was listed as not needing a serializer.  However,
    when used with an adapter storing the job arguments as JSON, it would get
    serialized as a simple String, resulting in deserialization also producing
    a String (instead of a BigDecimal).

    By using a serializer, we ensure the round trip is safe.

    To ensure applications using BigDecimal job arguments are not subject to
    race conditions during deployment (where a replica running a version of
    Rails without BigDecimalSerializer fails to deserialize an argument
    serialized with it), `ActiveJob.use_big_decimal_serializer` is disabled by
    default, and can be set to true in a following deployment..

    *Sam Bostock*

*   Preserve full-precision `enqueued_at` timestamps for serialized jobs,
## Rails 8.1.0 (October 22, 2025) ##

*   Add structured events for Active Job:
    - `active_job.enqueued`
    - `active_job.bulk_enqueued`
    - `active_job.started`
    - `active_job.completed`
    - `active_job.retry_scheduled`
    - `active_job.retry_stopped`
    - `active_job.discarded`
    - `active_job.interrupt`
    - `active_job.resume`
    - `active_job.step_skipped`
    - `active_job.step_started`
    - `active_job.step`

    *Adrianna Chang*

*   Deprecate built-in `sidekiq` adapter.

    If you're using this adapter, upgrade to `sidekiq` 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.

    *fatkodima*

*   Remove deprecated internal `SuckerPunch` adapter in favor of the adapter included with the `sucker_punch` gem.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove support to set `ActiveJob::Base.enqueue_after_transaction_commit` to `:never`, `:always` and `:default`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated `Rails.application.config.active_job.enqueue_after_transaction_commit`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   `ActiveJob::Serializers::ObjectSerializers#klass` method is now public.

    Custom Active Job serializers must have a public `#klass` method too.
    The returned class will be index allowing for faster serialization.

    *Jean Boussier*

*   Allow jobs to the interrupted and resumed with Continuations


    *Donal McBreen*

*   Defer invocation of ActiveJob enqueue callbacks until after commit when
    `enqueue_after_transaction_commit` is enabled.

    *Will Roever*

*   Add `report:` option to `ActiveJob::Base#retry_on` and `#discard_on`

    When the `report:` option is passed, errors will be reported to the error reporter
    before being retried / discarded.

    *Andrew Novoselac*

*   Accept a block for `ActiveJob::ConfiguredJob#perform_later`.

    This was inconsistent with a regular `ActiveJob::Base#perform_later`.

    *fatkodima*

*   Raise a more specific error during deserialization when a previously serialized job class is now unknown.

    `ActiveJob::UnknownJobClassError` will be raised instead of a more generic
    `NameError` to make it easily possible for adapters to tell if the `NameError`
    was raised during job execution or deserialization.

def retry_on(*exceptions, wait: 3.seconds, attempts: 5, queue: nil, priority: nil, jitter: JITTER_DEFAULT, report: false)
        rescue_from(*exceptions) do |error|
          executions = executions_for(exceptions)
          if attempts == :unlimited || executions < attempts
            ActiveSupport.error_reporter.report(error, source: "application.active_job") if report
            retry_job wait: determine_delay(seconds_or_duration_or_algorithm: wait, executions: executions, jitter: jitter), queue: queue, priority: priority, error: error
          else
            if block_given?
              instrument :retry_stopped, error: error do
                yield self, error
              end
              run_after_discard_procs(error)
            else
              instrument :retry_stopped, error: error
              run_after_discard_procs(error)
              raise error
            end
          end
        end
      end

module ActiveJob
  module EnqueueAfterTransactionCommit # :nodoc:
    private
      def raw_enqueue
        if self.class.enqueue_after_transaction_commit
          self.successfully_enqueued = true
          ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
            self.successfully_enqueued = false
            super
          end
          self

      end

      # :singleton-method:
      #
      # Defines if enqueueing this job from inside an Active Record transaction
      # automatically defers the enqueue to after the transaction commits.
      #
      # It can be set on a per job basis:
      #  - true forces the job to be deferred.
      #  - false forces the job to be queued immediately.
      class_attribute :enqueue_after_transaction_commit, instance_accessor: false, instance_predicate: false, default: false
    end

    # Includes the +perform_later+ method for job initialization.
    module ClassMethods
      # Push a job onto the queue. By default the arguments must be either String,
      # Integer, Float, NilClass, TrueClass, FalseClass, BigDecimal, Symbol, Date,
      # Time, DateTime, ActiveSupport::TimeWithZone, ActiveSupport::Duration,
      # Hash, ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess, Array, Range, or
      # GlobalID::Identification instances, although this can be extended by adding
      # custom serializers.
      #
      # Returns an instance of the job class queued with arguments available in
      # Job#arguments or +false+ if the enqueue did not succeed.
      #
      # After the attempted enqueue, the job will be yielded to an optional block.
      #
      # If Active Job is used conjointly with Active Record, and #perform_later is called
      # inside an Active Record transaction, then the enqueue is implicitly deferred to after
      # the transaction is committed, or dropped if it's rolled back. In such case #perform_later
      # will return the job instance like if it was successfully enqueued, but will still return
      # +false+ if a callback prevented the job from being enqueued.
      #
      # This behavior can be changed on a per job basis:
      #
      #  class NotificationJob < ApplicationJob
      #    self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = false
      #  end
      def perform_later(...)
        job = job_or_instantiate(...)
        enqueue_result = job.enqueue

        yield job if block_given?

        enqueue_result
      end

    class TimeWithZoneSerializer < ObjectSerializer # :nodoc:
      NANO_PRECISION = 9

gem "sidekiq", ">= 4.1.0"
require "sidekiq"

module ActiveJob
  module QueueAdapters
    class SidekiqAdapter < AbstractAdapter
      def initialize(*) # :nodoc:
        @stopping = false

        Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end

        Sidekiq.configure_client do |config|
          config.on(:quiet) { @stopping = true }
        end
      end

      def check_adapter
        ActiveJob.deprecator.warn <<~MSG.squish
          The built-in `sidekiq` adapter is deprecated and will be removed in Rails 8.2.
          Please upgrade `sidekiq` gem to version 7.3.3 or later to use the `sidekiq` gem's adapter.
        MSG
      end

      def enqueue(job) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name
        ).perform_async(job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_at(job, timestamp) # :nodoc:
        job.provider_job_id = JobWrapper.set(
          wrapped: job.class,
          queue: job.queue_name,
        ).perform_at(timestamp, job.serialize)
      end

      def enqueue_all(jobs) # :nodoc:
        enqueued_count = 0
        jobs.group_by(&:class).each do |job_class, same_class_jobs|
          same_class_jobs.group_by(&:queue_name).each do |queue, same_class_and_queue_jobs|
            immediate_jobs, scheduled_jobs = same_class_and_queue_jobs.partition { |job| job.scheduled_at.nil? }

            if immediate_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => immediate_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end

            if scheduled_jobs.any?
              jids = Sidekiq::Client.push_bulk(
                "class" => JobWrapper,
                "wrapped" => job_class,
                "queue" => queue,
                "args" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| [job.serialize] },
                "at" => scheduled_jobs.map { |job| job.scheduled_at&.to_f }
              )
              enqueued_count += jids.compact.size
            end
          end
        end
        enqueued_count
      end

      class JobWrapper # :nodoc:
        include Sidekiq::Worker

        def perform(job_data)
          Base.execute job_data.merge("provider_job_id" => jid)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

This indexes the association validation errors based on the order received by nested attributes setter, and respects the `reject_if` configuration. This enables API to provide enough information to the frontend to map the validation errors back to their respective form fields.

    *lulalala*

*   Add `Rails.application.config.active_record.postgresql_adapter_decode_dates` to opt out of decoding dates automatically with the postgresql adapter. Defaults to true.

    *Joé Dupuis*

*   Association option `query_constraints` is deprecated in favor of `foreign_key`.

    *Nikita Vasilevsky*

*   Add `ENV["SKIP_TEST_DATABASE_TRUNCATE"]` flag to speed up multi-process test runs on large DBs when all tests run within default transaction.

    This cuts ~10s from the test run of HEY when run by 24 processes against the 178 tables, since ~4,000 table truncates can then be skipped.
    end
    ```

    *Cody Cutrer*

*   `PostgreSQLAdapter` now decodes columns of type date to `Date` instead of string.

    Ex:
    ```ruby
    ActiveRecord::Base.connection
         .select_value("select '2024-01-01'::date").class #=> Date
    ```

    *Joé Dupuis*

*   Strict loading using `:n_plus_one_only` does not eagerly load child associations.

    With this change, child associations are no longer eagerly loaded, to
    match intended behavior and to prevent non-deterministic order issues caused
    by calling methods like `first` or `last`. As `first` and `last` don't cause
    an N+1 by themselves, calling child associations will no longer raise.
    them from the database again.

    *Adam Hess*

*   Deprecate `read_attribute(:id)` returning the primary key if the primary key is not `:id`.

    Starting in Rails 7.2, `read_attribute(:id)` will return the value of the id column, regardless of the model's
    primary key. To retrieve the value of the primary key, use `#id` instead. `read_attribute(:id)` for composite
    primary key models will now return the value of the id column.

    *Adrianna Chang*

*   Fix `change_table` setting datetime precision for 6.1 Migrations

    *Hartley McGuire*

*   Fix change_column setting datetime precision for 6.1 Migrations

    *Hartley McGuire*

*   Add `ActiveRecord::Base#id_value` alias to access the raw value of a record's id column.

    This alias is only provided for models that declare an `:id` column.

    *Adrianna Chang*

*   Deprecate `rewhere` argument on `#merge`.

    The `rewhere` argument on `#merge`is deprecated without replacement and
    will be removed in Rails 7.2.

    *Adam Hess*

*   Deprecate aliasing non-attributes with `alias_attribute`.

    *Ian Candy*

*   Fix unscope is not working in specific case

    Before:
    ```ruby
    Post.where(id: 1...3).unscope(where: :id).to_sql # "SELECT `posts`.* FROM `posts` WHERE `posts`.`id` >= 1 AND `posts`.`id` < 3"

    ```

    After:
    ```ruby
    Post.where(id: 1...3).unscope(where: :id).to_sql # "SELECT `posts`.* FROM `posts`"
    ```

    Fixes #48094.

*   `ActiveRecord::Base.serialize` no longer uses YAML by default.

    YAML isn't particularly performant and can lead to security issues
    if not used carefully.

    Unfortunately there isn't really any good serializers in Ruby's stdlib
    to replace it.

    The obvious choice would be JSON, which is a fine format for this use case,
    however the JSON serializer in Ruby's stdlib isn't strict enough, as it fallback
    to casting unknown types to strings, which could lead to corrupted data.

    Some third party JSON libraries like `Oj` have a suitable strict mode.

    So it's preferable that users choose a serializer based on their own constraints.

    The original default can be restored by setting `config.active_record.default_column_serializer = YAML`.

    *Jean Boussier*

*   `ActiveRecord::Base.serialize` signature changed.

    Rather than a single positional argument that accepts two possible
    types of values, `serialize` now accepts two distinct keyword arguments.

    Before:

    ```ruby
    serialize :content, JSON
    serialize :backtrace, Array
    ```

    After:

    ```ruby
    serialize :content, coder: JSON
    serialize :backtrace, type: Array
    ```

    *Jean Boussier*

    same notation as the `build` method on associations.

    *Sean Denny*

*   Raise on assignment to readonly attributes

    ```ruby
    class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
      attr_readonly :content
    end
    Post.create!(content: "cannot be updated")
    post.content # "cannot be updated"
    post.content = "something else" # => ActiveRecord::ReadonlyAttributeError
    ```

    Previously, assignment would succeed but silently not write to the database.
*   Fix `ActiveRecord::Store` to serialize as a regular Hash

    Previously it would serialize as an `ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess`
    which is wasteful and cause problem with YAML safe_load.

    *Jean Boussier*

*   Add `timestamptz` as a time zone aware type for PostgreSQL
    ```

    *Petrik de Heus*

*   Bring back the historical behavior of committing transaction on non-local return.

    ```ruby
    Model.transaction do
      model.save
      return
      other_model.save # not executed
    end
    ```

    Historically only raised errors would trigger a rollback, but in Ruby `2.3`, the `timeout` library
    started using `throw` to interrupt execution which had the adverse effect of committing open transactions.

    To solve this, in Active Record 6.1 the behavior was changed to instead rollback the transaction as it was safer
    than to potentially commit an incomplete transaction.

    Using `return`, `break` or `throw` inside a `transaction` block was essentially deprecated from Rails 6.1 onwards.
*   Fix `has_one` association autosave setting the foreign key attribute when it is unchanged.

    This behavior is also inconsistent with autosaving `belongs_to` and can have unintended side effects like raising
    an `ActiveRecord::ReadonlyAttributeError` when the foreign key attribute is marked as read-only.

    *Joshua Young*

*   Remove deprecated behavior that would rollback a transaction block when exited using `return`, `break` or `throw`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Deprecate `Rails.application.config.active_record.commit_transaction_on_non_local_return`.

    *Rafael Mendonça França*

*   Remove deprecated support to pass `rewhere` to `ActiveRecord::Relation#merge`.

require "test_helper" class ImportsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest setup { sign_in_as users(:reader) } test "previews a CSV without saving, then imports every row and offers a receipt" do notebook = notebooks(:essays) csv = <<~CSV title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch On idleness,

Idle minds

,10.1000/Essays.1,Read twice & reflect,1767225600 "Of experience","

Long essay

",10.1000/Essays.1,Compare with Bacon, CSV assert_no_changes -> { record_counts } do post notebook_import_preview_path(notebook), params: { import: { file: upload(csv) } } end assert_response :success assert_select "#line_2 h2", "Line 2: On idleness" assert_select "#line_2 dd", "Read twice & reflect" assert_select "#line_4 h2", "Line 4: Of experience" assert_select "#line_4 dd", "Compare with Bacon" assert_select "#line_2 time[datetime=?]", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" csv_field = css_select("input[type=hidden][name='import[csv]']").first["value"] assert_difference -> { Note.count } => 2, -> { Citation.count } => 1, -> { Import.count } => 1 do post notebook_imports_path(notebook), params: { import: { csv: csv_field } } end import = Import.last assert_redirected_to notebook_import_path(notebook, import) idleness, experience = import.notes.order(:id) assert_equal [notebook, notebook], [idleness.notebook, experience.notebook] assert_equal ["Read twice & reflect", 1767225600], [idleness.annotation, idleness.reminder_epoch] assert_equal ["Compare with Bacon", nil], [experience.annotation, experience.reminder_epoch] get note_path(idleness) assert_select ".trix-content b", "minds" assert_select ".citation dd", text: "Read twice & reflect" get notebook_import_path(notebook, import, format: :csv) assert_equal "text/csv", response.media_type assert_equal "title,doi\nOn idleness,10.1000/Essays.1\nOf experience,10.1000/Essays.1\n", response.body end test "invalid rows are shown with their errors, and applying them saves nothing" do notebook = notebooks(:novels) csv = <<~CSV title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch Adam Bede,

Hayslope

,10.1000/bede,First reading, ,

Untitled

,not-a-doi,Second reading,tomorrow CSV post notebook_import_preview_path(notebook), params: { import: { file: upload(csv) } } assert_response :unprocessable_entity assert_select "#line_3 .row-errors li", "Title can't be blank" assert_select "#line_3 .row-errors li", "DOI is invalid" assert_select "#line_3 .row-errors li", "Reminder epoch is not a number" assert_select "#line_3 dd", "Second reading" assert_select "input[name='import[csv]']", count: 0 assert_no_changes -> { record_counts } do post notebook_imports_path(notebook), params: { import: { csv: csv } } end assert_response :unprocessable_entity assert_select "#line_2 .row-errors", count: 0 assert_select "#line_3 .row-errors li", "Title can't be blank" assert_nil Note.find_by(title: "Adam Bede") end test "rejects a missing CSV or one without the documented header row" do post notebook_import_preview_path(notebooks(:novels)), params: { import: { file: upload("name,doi\nAdam Bede,10.1000/bede\n") } } assert_response :unprocessable_entity assert_select ".errors li", "CSV file must start with the header row title,body_html,doi,annotation,reminder_epoch"

def serialize(attr_name, coder: nil, type: Object, comparable: false, yaml: {}, **options)
          coder ||= default_column_serializer
          unless coder
            raise ArgumentError, <<~MSG.squish
              missing keyword: :coder

              If no default coder is configured, a coder must be provided to `serialize`.
            MSG
          end

          column_serializer = build_column_serializer(attr_name, coder, type, yaml)

          attribute(attr_name, **options)

          decorate_attributes([attr_name]) do |attr_name, cast_type|
            if type_incompatible_with_serialize?(cast_type, coder, type)
              raise ColumnNotSerializableError.new(attr_name, cast_type)
            end

            cast_type = cast_type.subtype if Type::Serialized === cast_type
            Type::Serialized.new(cast_type, column_serializer, comparable: comparable)
          end
        end

        private
          def build_column_serializer(attr_name, coder, type, yaml = nil)
            # When ::JSON is used, force it to go through the Active Support JSON encoder
            # to ensure special objects (e.g. Active Record models) are dumped correctly
            # using the #as_json hook.

            if coder == ::JSON || coder == Coders::JSON
              coder = Coders::JSON.new
            end

            if coder == ::YAML || coder == Coders::YAMLColumn
              Coders::YAMLColumn.new(attr_name, type, **(yaml || {}))
            elsif coder.respond_to?(:new) && !coder.respond_to?(:load)
              coder.new(attr_name, type)
            elsif type && type != Object
              Coders::ColumnSerializer.new(attr_name, coder, type)
            else
              coder
            end
          end

          def type_incompatible_with_serialize?(cast_type, coder, type)
            cast_type.is_a?(ActiveRecord::Type::Json) && coder == ::JSON ||
              cast_type.respond_to?(:type_cast_array, true) && type == ::Array

    structured (e.g., PostgreSQL +hstore+/+json+, or MySQL +json+) or declared serializable via
    `ActiveRecord.store`.

        NoMethodError: undefined method `accessor' for an instance of ActiveRecord::Type::Text

    Now, a descriptive `ConfigurationError` is raised:

content.content:
*   Add comprehensive support for HTTP Cache-Control request directives according to RFC 9111.

    Provides a `request.cache_control_directives` object that gives access to request cache directives:

    ```ruby
    # Boolean directives
    request.cache_control_directives.only_if_cached?  # => true/false
    request.cache_control_directives.no_cache?        # => true/false
    request.cache_control_directives.no_store?        # => true/false
    request.cache_control_directives.no_transform?    # => true/false

    # Value directives
    request.cache_control_directives.max_age          # => integer or nil
    request.cache_control_directives.max_stale        # => integer or nil (or true for valueless max-stale)
    request.cache_control_directives.min_fresh        # => integer or nil
    request.cache_control_directives.stale_if_error   # => integer or nil

    # Special helpers for max-stale
    request.cache_control_directives.max_stale?         # => true if max-stale present (with or without value)
    request.cache_control_directives.max_stale_unlimited? # => true only for valueless max-stale
    ```

    Example usage:

    ```ruby
    def show
      if request.cache_control_directives.only_if_cached?
        @article = Article.find_cached(params[:id])
        return head(:gateway_timeout) if @article.nil?
      else
        @article = Article.find(params[:id])
      end

      render :show
    end
    ```

    *egg528*

*   Add assert_in_body/assert_not_in_body as the simplest way to check if a piece of text is in the response body.

*   Make `http_cache_forever` use `immutable: true`

    *Nate Matykiewicz*

*   Add `config.action_dispatch.strict_freshness`.

    When set to `true`, the `ETag` header takes precedence over the `Last-Modified` header when both are present,
    as specified by RFC 7232, Section 6.

    Defaults to `false` to maintain compatibility with previous versions of Rails, but is enabled as part of
    Rails 8.0 defaults.

    *heka1024*

*   Support `immutable` directive in Cache-Control

*   Parse all three HTTP-date formats in the `If-Modified-Since` request header.

    `If-Modified-Since` carries an HTTP-date, which RFC 9110 allows in any of
    three formats (IMF-fixdate, RFC 850, or asctime), and requires recipients to
    accept all three. The header was parsed with `Time.rfc2822`, which only
    accepts the IMF-fixdate format, and the parse failure was swallowed — so a
    conditional `GET` using an RFC 850 or asctime date silently failed to produce
    a `304 Not Modified` and re-sent the full response. It is now parsed with
    `Time.httpdate`, consistent with how `Last-Modified` and `Date` are read.

    *Kenta Ishizaki*

input.description: Check Integer type casting changes

content.content:
*   Fix `ActiveModel::Type::BigInteger` truncating strings longer than 16 bytes when casting.

    `BigInteger` (and Active Record decimal columns without a scale) now limits
    the cast string to twice its `precision`, or to 2000 bytes when it has none.

    *Suliman Abdulrazzaq*

*   Limit the size of strings `ActiveModel::Type::Integer` will coerce with `to_i`.

    Calling `to_i` on very long strings can take a long time and could be used as
    a DoS vector. Integer casting now only considers the first `_limit * 4` bytes
    of a string (16 bytes for a default 4-byte integer, 32 bytes for an 8-byte
    bigint), which is enough to hold the maximum representable value plus a sign
    or a short slug suffix.

    *Aaron Patterson*, *Jean Boussier*

*   Fix `ActiveSupport::Duration#in_minutes`, `#in_hours`, `#in_days`,
    `#in_weeks`, `#in_months`, and `#in_years` truncating sub-second precision.

    These methods divided the duration's integer second count (`in_seconds`,
    aliased to `to_i`) instead of its exact value, so any fractional second was
    silently dropped before the conversion.

    ```ruby
    # Before
    90.5.seconds.in_minutes # => 1.5

    # After
    90.5.seconds.in_minutes # => 1.5083333333333333
    ```

    *Kenta Ishizaki*

require "sidekiq/job"

module Sidekiq
  class Rails < ::Rails::Engine
    class Reloader
      def initialize(app = ::Rails.application)
        @app = app
      end

      def call
        @app.reloader.wrap do
          yield
        end
      end

      def inspect
        "#<Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader @app=#{@app.class.name}>"
      end
    end

    initializer "sidekiq.active_job_integration" do
      ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_job) do
        include ::Sidekiq::Job::Options unless respond_to?(:sidekiq_options)
      end
    end

    config.before_configuration do
      dep = ActiveSupport::Deprecation.new("7.0", "Sidekiq")
      dep.deprecate_methods(Sidekiq.singleton_class,
        default_worker_options: :default_job_options,
        "default_worker_options=": :default_job_options=)
    end

    config.after_initialize do
      Sidekiq.configure_server do |config|
        config[:reloader] = Sidekiq::Rails::Reloader.new

        unless ::Rails.logger == config.logger || ::ActiveSupport::Logger.logger_outputs_to?(::Rails.logger, $stdout)
          if ::Rails::VERSION::STRING < "7.1"
            ::Rails.logger.extend(::ActiveSupport::Logger.broadcast(config.logger))
          else
            ::Rails.logger.broadcast_to(config.logger)
          end
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

content.text:
I rated 6 changes high, 6 medium and 10 low. Ten changes alter behavior or break code that this app actually uses.

Several of the high-risk changes don't raise any error in production. The existing tests should catch five of the six. I compared the unpacked 7.0.8.7 and 8.1.0 gems and the 7.1, 7.2, 8.0 and 8.1.0 changelogs. Nothing in the app was installed, changed or run. Each claim is tagged **[changelog]**, **[code]** (gem or app source I read) or **[inference]**.

## Facts about the app these ratings depend on

- **Framework defaults stay at 7.0.** `config.load_defaults 7.0` (config/application.rb:12) is assumed to stay. M6 lists what breaks if you raise it.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL only (pg 1.6.0).
- **Background jobs:** Active Job uses `:sidekiq` (config/application.rb:24) with Sidekiq 6.5.12 and redis 4.8.1. Tests use `:test`. `ExportJob` is a plain Sidekiq job.
- **Rolling deploys:** I assume old and new workers can share Redis during a deploy. If you stop every worker first, the mixed-version part of H4 doesn't apply.
- **Caching:** production has caching on and no `cache_store` set, so it uses the default file store. Tests use the null store with caching off.
- **Front end:** HTML only (ERB, Sprockets, importmap, Turbo). Action Text runs with a vendored Trix 1.3.5 loaded as a classic script. Active Storage uses the local disk.
- **Not used:** JSON responses, Action Cable channels, Action Mailbox, Active Record encryption.
- **Time zones:** `users.time_zone` stores Rails zone names like "Eastern Time (US & Canada)".
- **Dependencies:** Rails 8.1 accepts your current pins (Ruby 3.3.6, rack 2.2.24, concurrent-ruby 1.3.4, minitest ~> 5.25, pg). It adds action_text-trix (~> 2.1.15), rack-session, rackup and useragent. **[code: gemspec metadata]**

## High

**H1. Leaving a transaction with `return` now commits instead of rolling back (7.2)**
- **Before:** if the block had written anything and exited early, Rails rolled back. **[code: old transaction.rb:336-342]**
- **Now:** it commits. **[code: new transaction.rb:655-668]** **[changelog: [7-2-stable activerecord](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md), "Remove deprecated behavior that would rollback…", PR #48600]**
- **Where:** `app/models/import.rb:53-58` has `return false unless row.note.save` inside `transaction do`.
- **What could go wrong:** if any row fails during apply, the import and the rows before it are saved. Meanwhile the controller shows the preview again with a 422 (`imports_controller.rb:12-19`). Submitting again creates duplicates. ARCHITECTURE.md promises the opposite. The test at `test/controllers/imports_controller_test.rb:48-72` should catch it.

**H2. `record[:id]` no longer returns a custom primary key (7.2)**
- **Before:** `read_attribute(:id)` returned the primary key.
- **Now:** it reads a column literally named `id`. `citations` has none, so the result is `nil`. **[code: new read.rb:29-34, attribute_set.rb]** **[changelog: PR #49019, removed in 7.2]**
- **Where:** `app/models/import.rb:68` (`citation && citation[:id]`).
- **What could go wrong:** the receipt CSV's DOI column comes out silently blank. The test at `imports_controller_test.rb:44-45` should catch it.

**H3. `HashWithIndifferentAccess#stringify_keys` now converts every key to a string (8.0)**
- **Before:** it only converted symbol keys, so integer keys stayed integers.
- **Now:** integer keys become strings. **[changelog: PR #53125]** **[code: the override was removed]**
- **Where:**
  - `app/models/import.rb:38-42` keys annotations by integer line number.
  - `app/views/imports/preview.html.erb:22` calls `.stringify_keys`.
  - Line 42 then looks them up with an integer.
- **What could go wrong:** annotations silently disappear from the import preview. The test at `imports_controller_test.rb:21-24` should catch it.

**H4. Active Job keeps a time's zone, and BigDecimal job arguments use a new format (7.1.3 / 7.2)**
- **Before:** a time with zone was rebuilt in the worker's zone (UTC). A BigDecimal was sent as a plain string.
- **Now:**
  - The serializer stores the zone name and the job rebuilds the time in the reader's zone.
  - BigDecimal has its own serializer. **[code: new time_with_zone_serializer.rb, big_decimal_serializer.rb]** **[changelog: [7-1-stable activejob](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md) 7.1.3; [7-2-stable activejob](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md) "Remove deprecated primitive serializer for BigDecimal"; PR #45618]**
- **Where:**
  - `app/models/user.rb:35,41` enqueues the digest job.
  - `app/jobs/digest_job.rb:6-7` passes the time through.
  - `app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:8-9` uses `requested_at.to_date` and `.all_day`.
- **What could go wrong (one version running):** for non-UTC readers, the digest's date and note list follow their local day. That no longer matches the UTC reservation key (`user.rb:36`) or the "today (UTC)" hint (`notes/index.html.erb:10`). The test at `digests_controller_test.rb` (subject "October 05, 2026") should catch it. `BigDecimal(params[:completion])` keeps working. **[inference]**
- **What could go wrong (old and new running together):**
  - A 7.0 worker cannot load a digest job queued by 8.1, because of the BigDecimal format. It raises `DeserializationError`, and since there's no `discard_on`, Sidekiq retries it, so the digest is late.
  - Jobs queued by 7.0 still deserialize in UTC under 8.1.

  **[inference from code]**

**H5. `TimeWithZone#to_time` now keeps the zone, not just the offset (8.0 / 8.1)**
- **Before:** the result had a fixed offset (`getlocal(utc_offset)`).
- **Now:** it is `getlocal(time_zone)`, so adding seconds recalculates the offset. **[code: new time_with_zone.rb:497-498]** **[changelog: [8.1.0 activesupport](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/v8.1.0/activesupport/CHANGELOG.md) "Remove deprecated support for `to_time`…"]**
- **Where:** `app/models/note.rb:43-45`, displayed at `app/views/notes/_reminder.html.erb:19`.
- **What could go wrong:** across a daylight-saving change, the "24 hours later" preview now shows the new offset and wall-clock time (e.g. `08:00-05:00` instead of `09:00-04:00`). The moment in time is the same. This arguably fixes a quirk ARCHITECTURE.md documents, but it changes output silently. The test at `reminders_controller_test.rb:21` asserts the old value.

**H6. Some Rails time-zone names map to different tz zones (7.2)**
- **The change:**
  - "Astana" changes from Asia/Dhaka to Asia/Almaty.
  - "Canberra" now maps to Australia/Canberra and "Greenland" to America/Nuuk.
  - "Asuncion" is new.

  **[code: diff of values/time_zone.rb]** **[changelog: 7-2-stable activesupport]**
- **Where:** `user.rb:13,22`, `note.rb:37`, `accounts/edit.html.erb:15`.
- **What could go wrong:** readers set to "Astana" would likely get UTC+5 instead of +6. Their entered and displayed reminder times would shift by an hour. Already-scheduled jobs keep their stored times. Canberra and Greenland follow the same rules as before. **[inference]**
- **To check:** count users with `time_zone = 'Astana'`.

## Medium

**M1. `Rails.application.secrets` is removed (deprecated 7.1, removed 7.2)**
- **The change:** `config/secrets.yml` is now silently ignored. **[code: no `secrets` in new railties]** **[changelog: 7-2-stable railties]**
- **Where:**
  - `app/models/citation/provider.rb:13` raises `NoMethodError` inside the job.
  - The tests use it at `citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:45,117-122`.
- **The decision:** choose a replacement, such as `config_for`, credentials, or reading ENV directly.
  - Encrypted credentials can't read ENV.
  - Whichever you choose must still quote values like `"00123"` and `"sample: value # keep"`, which the `.to_json` in secrets.yml does today.

**M2. `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` now starts as `nil` (7.1)**
- **The change:** `config/initializers/action_text.rb:3` (`+=`) raises `NoMethodError` at boot. **[code: new content_helper.rb:10,68-70]** **[changelog: 7-1-stable actiontext]**
- **The decision:** the fix has to rebuild the whole list, for example `sanitizer.class.allowed_tags + [ActionText::Attachment.tag_name, "figure", "figcaption", "details", "summary"]`. If any of those defaults is left out, rendered rich text silently loses its attachments.

**M3. Rails' built-in Sidekiq adapter is deprecated (8.1), and Rails 8.2 removes it**
- **The change:** the adapter still works with Sidekiq 6.5.12. **[code: new sidekiq_adapter.rb]** **[changelog: 8.1.0 activejob, PR #53058]**
- **Where:** `config/application.rb:24`.
- **The decision:** moving to Sidekiq 7.3.3 or later replaces redis-rb with redis-client. That would likely break two things:
  - `redis.sadd` at `user.rb:38` would return an Integer, which is always truthy, so the once-per-day digest check would stop working.
  - The `rescue Redis::BaseError` at `notebook.rb:28` would stop matching Redis errors.

  **[inference]**

**M4. Trix 2 now comes from the `action_text-trix` gem (8.1)**
- **The change:**
  - `*= require trix` in `app/assets/stylesheets/actiontext.css:6` now loads Trix 2.1.15's CSS, while `layouts/application.html.erb:13` still loads the vendored Trix 1.3.5 JavaScript.
  - `config/importmap.rb:8` points at `actiontext.js`, which is now a UMD build. Rails 7.1+ ships `actiontext.esm.js` for import maps.

  **[code]** **[changelog: 8.1.0 actiontext]**
- **What could go wrong:** the editor's styling won't match its JavaScript, with no error raised. It needs checking in a browser.
- **The decision:** adopt Trix 2, or keep 1.3.5 together with its own CSS.

**M5. A negative cache `expires_in` is now dropped and logged as an error (7.1)**
- **Where:** `app/views/exports/_export.html.erb:26` (`export.expires_at - Time.current`).
- **What changes:** for an export that has already expired, the "Expired" fragment is now cached with no expiry, and each such write logs an `ArgumentError`. What users see stays correct. **[code: new cache.rb:922-925]** **[inference on impact]**
- **What could go wrong:** with the 7.1 default `raise_on_invalid_cache_expiration_time = true`, the exports page would raise instead. Tests don't run with caching on, so they won't notice.

**M6. Newer framework defaults that would break this app if you raise `load_defaults`** **[code: railties configuration.rb]**
- **7.1 `raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly`:** every notebook settings save raises, because the form resubmits the read-only `slug` (`notebooks_controller.rb:40`, `notebooks/_form.html.erb:13`). It raises even when the value is unchanged (`readonly_attributes.rb:49-63`).
- **7.1 `default_column_serializer = nil`:** `serialize :preferences` (`notebook.rb:7`) raises unless you add `coder: YAML`.
- **7.1 HTML5 sanitizer:** changes which tags rich text keeps.
- **7.1 cache and message format versions:** old Rails can't read the new format, which matters if you roll back.
- **7.2 `postgresql_adapter_decode_dates`:** `Date.iso8601(Date)` at `notebook.rb:40` raises a `TypeError`, so the activity page fails.
- **8.0 `strict_freshness`:** `ETag` takes precedence over `Last-Modified` in `export_downloads_controller.rb:11`.

## Low (each raises an error, and tests or boot should catch it)
- **`serialize :tags, JSON`:** change to `coder: JSON` (`note.rb:12`). Removed in 7.2.
- **Keyword-style enum:** `enum status: …, _prefix: true` becomes `enum :status, {…}, prefix: true` (`note.rb:10`). Removed in 8.0.
- **`alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color`:** raises because `color` is a store accessor, not an attribute. Use `alias_method` for the reader and writer (`note.rb:14`). Removed in 7.2.
- **`wait: :exponentially_longer`:** raises only when a retry happens. Rename it to `:polynomially_longer` (`citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`). Removed in 7.2.
- **`set(wait_until: reminder_epoch)` with an Integer:** raises `NoMethodError` (`#utc`). Wrap it in `Time.at` (`note.rb:61`). Removed in 7.2.
- **`fragments.sum` on strings:** now raises `TypeError`. Use `join` (`export.rb:42`). Removed in 7.1; the exports test drains the job and will catch it.
- **A route with two paths:** `get "/notes", "/journal"` raises `ArgumentError`. Split it into two routes (`routes.rb:18`). Removed in 8.1, PR #52409.
- **`form_with(model: nil, …)`:** raises. Drop `model: nil` (`notes/index.html.erb:12`). Removed in 8.0.
- **`show_exceptions = false`:** is now treated as `:all`, so the 23 `assert_raises` in tests fail. Use `:none` (`environments/test.rb:31`). Removed in 7.2.
- **Development secret file:** moves from `tmp/development_secret.txt` to `tmp/local_secret.txt`. Dev sessions reset, and attachments already stored in dev rich text stop resolving. Dev only.
- **Action Text plain-text conversion rewritten (no error raised):** `<script>` and `<style>` text is now dropped, and ordered-list numbers are counted from list items only. Export Markdown and note excerpts may differ slightly. **[code]**

## Not relevant
- **MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy changes:** the app uses PostgreSQL.
- **Composite primary keys and encryption:** not used. Only H2 touches the DOI primary key.
- **`enqueue_after_transaction_commit`:** stays off by default in 8.1. Don't turn it on: `request_enrichment` and `schedule_reminder` rely on queuing jobs inside the lock.
- **Redis, Memcache and Solid Cache store changes:** the app uses the file, memory and null stores.
- **Action Cable, Action Mailbox, cloud Active Storage services and image variants:** not used.
- **JSON rendering and escaping changes, and the new `remote_ip` rules:** the app has no JSON responses and doesn't read `remote_ip`.
- **Rack 3 changes:** the app stays on rack 2.2.
- **Generator-only features:** Solid Queue/Cable/Cache, Kamal, Propshaft, the authentication generator, `bin/ci`.

ARCHITECTURE.md describes several of the old behaviors (UTC digest days, the offset in the reminder preview, Trix 1.3.5, secrets.yml). Update it once you decide on each.

Everything I compared is in `/tmp/gemcmp`:
- `/tmp/gemcmp/old` and `/tmp/gemcmp/new`: the unpacked 7.0.8.7 and 8.1.0 gems.
- `/tmp/gemcmp/cl`: the changelogs. The 7-2-stable and 8-0-stable files also include releases made after 8.1.0; I checked the 8.1.0 source wherever that mattered.
- `/tmp/gemcmp/sk`: Sidekiq 6.5.12.
- `/tmp/gemcmp/trix`: action_text-trix 2.1.15.
- `/tmp/gemcmp/mid`: Active Job 7.2.2 and 8.0.3.
